issues.description: The Lecture class fields are declared with snake_case identifiers in the solution (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while the constructor and methods in the same solution file reference camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The problem statement (UML) also uses the camelCase names. This naming mismatch (declaration vs. usage) will cause compilation errors and prevents students from mapping the UML/description to the code unambiguously.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the field names consistent with the UML and method usages. Rename the declared fields in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to the camelCase names used throughout the constructor and methods: private String lectureName; private int numberOfInscribedStudents; private int numberOfGuestStudents; private int numberOfLecturers; private int numberOfTutors; Alternatively, change all constructor and method references to match the declared snake_case names—but prefer aligning declarations to the UML/camelCase identifiers so the template, solution and problem statement are consistent.
